claims.text: The overall high-temperature wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coatings is primarily governed by formation of a copper-rich protective oxide scale.
High-temperature exposure causes copper to segregate toward the FeNiCrCoCu coating surface.
Segregated copper oxidizes preferentially relative to the other coating constituents.
The resulting copper-rich oxide is dense and lubricious.
The copper-rich oxide reduces direct metal-to-metal contact during sliding.
The oxide barrier reduces friction and abrasive wear.
The oxide scale protects the underlying coating against further oxidation and mechanical degradation.
Pre-oxidation at approximately 800 °C promotes formation of a copper-enriched surface oxide.
Elevated-temperature treatment may also produce local phase segregation in the coating.
Pre-oxidized FeNiCrCoCu coatings will have a significantly lower high-temperature wear rate than as-deposited coatings tested under the same conditions.
Pre-oxidized FeNiCrCoCu coatings will have a lower coefficient of friction than the as-deposited baseline.
A continuous copper-enriched oxide scale will be present on pre-oxidized samples.
The proposed protective effect operates within approximately 600–800 °C.
Temperatures substantially above 800 °C or extreme mechanical loads may compromise oxide-scale integrity and alter wear behavior.
The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a homogeneous microstructure.
